title: QUIZ - 88
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.concept: Comparing Growth Models at a Specific Point
questions.learningObjective: Compare a linear and an exponential model's values at a specific input
questions.question: Linear model: L(t) = 41 + 9t. Exponential model: \(E(t) = 1 \times 2^t\). At t = 2, which model gives a larger value?

options.label: A
options.text: E (exponential)

options.label: B
options.text: This cannot be determined without a graph.

options.label: C
options.text: L (linear)

options.label: D
options.text: Both models give the same value at this point.

questions.explanation: At t = 2: \(L(2) = 41 + 9(2) = 59. E(2) = 1 \times 2^{2} = 4\). Comparing these values shows which is larger at this specific point.
questions.hint: Evaluate both models at the given input and compare the resulting values directly.

questions.concept: Graphical Differences Between Linear and Exponential Growth
questions.learningObjective: Recognize the graphical distinction between linear and exponential growth
questions.question: What shape characteristic distinguishes exponential growth from linear growth on a graph?

options.label: A
options.text: The exponential graph curves upward with increasing steepness, while the linear graph is a straight line.

options.label: B
options.text: Both graphs are straight lines, but with different slopes.

options.label: C
options.text: The exponential graph is a straight line, while the linear graph curves.

options.label: D
options.text: The exponential graph is always a horizontal line.

questions.explanation: A linear function has a constant rate of change, producing a straight line, whereas exponential growth has an increasing rate of change, producing an upward-curving graph.
questions.hint: Consider how the rate of change behaves for each type of function as the input increases.

questions.concept: Long-Term Behavior of Exponential vs. Linear Growth
questions.learningObjective: Recognize that exponential growth eventually overtakes linear growth for large inputs
questions.question: For sufficiently large inputs, which type of growth wins out: exponential or linear?

options.label: A
options.text: They grow at the same rate once the input is large enough.

options.label: B
options.text: Exponential growth will always eventually exceed linear growth, regardless of the starting values or rates.

options.label: C
options.text: Linear growth will always eventually exceed exponential growth.

options.label: D
options.text: It depends only on which one has the larger starting value.

questions.explanation: No matter the constants involved, an exponential function with base greater than 1 eventually grows faster than any linear function as the input increases without bound.
questions.hint: Think about what happens as the input becomes very large: multiplying repeatedly versus adding repeatedly.
